script:
Zhang Qingzhu
Zhang Qingzhu is an ordinary person who is somewhat materialistic, which is why she has never found a suitable partner. Once, she visited Fengbo Temple outside the city and discovered that the temple had flourishing incense offerings and high fees, realizing it must be making considerable money, which made her quite envious. While wandering around the temple, she met Abbot Yankong of Fengbo Temple and chatted with him briefly. Half-jokingly, she asked if he was wealthy, and unexpectedly, Yankong didn't avoid the question but even bragged to her about it. Zhang Qingzhu felt this abbot wasn't truly devoted to Buddhism, so she often came to Fengbo Temple to chat with Yankong. As time passed and their conversations deepened, Yankong even proposed to keep her as his mistress.
Zhang Qingzhu didn't refuse this opportunity for advancement. In her view, love was worthless compared to money. Yankong arranged for her to live in Quchenju, a residence for lay disciples, where he would meet her privately at night and regularly give her substantial amounts of money. Zhang Qingzhu was very satisfied with this lifestyle.
During her idle time, Zhang Qingzhu befriended another woman about her age at Quchenju named Li Xinyue. The two often chatted together and got along very well. However, Li Xinyue was somewhat timid and afraid of trouble, and still yearned for happy love, though it was said her husband had died long ago. Sometimes when Zhang Qingzhu said money was more important, Li Xinyue would advise her to take these material possessions lightly, which made Zhang Qingzhu find it rather boring.
In her interactions with Yankong, Zhang Qingzhu discovered that Yankong deeply loved his disciple Hengming. Hengming was about 20 years younger than both Yankong and herself, and was the most talented among those of the Heng generation. Sometimes when Zhang Qingzhu prepared vegetarian meals for Yankong, he would call Hengming to join them. Despite being someone who only used religion to make money, he was so fond of a disciple who merely had talent in Buddhist teachings, which Zhang Qingzhu found hard to understand. In Zhang Qingzhu's eyes, Hengming always seemed indifferent toward Yankong. However, Hengming seemed to share Yankong's interest in pets, as Zhang Qingzhu often saw him walking his dog around the temple.
A year ago, a wealthy merchant named Zhao Zhengwei moved into Quchenju, which greatly interested Zhang Qingzhu. This man was much wealthier than Yankong, was reportedly still single, and unlike Yankong, wasn't a monk who couldn't give her status. Zhang Qingzhu approached Zhao Zhengwei, but he completely ignored her. After a couple of attempts, Zhang Qingzhu stopped embarrassing herself.
But Zhao Zhengwei's purpose for moving in aroused Zhang Qingzhu's interest. After some investigation, she finally discovered that Yankong and he were doing business together using Fengbo Temple, and the amounts involved were enormous. She secretly recorded the account details and found that the money Yankong gave her was nothing compared to these sums, even though Yankong told her he was giving her most of his income. She became dissatisfied and hoped to get more money.
On July 25th, she confronted Yankong with these account records, demanding more money. Having no choice, Yankong told Zhang Qingzhu that if she helped him with one favor, she could get the money. Yankong said that his peer Yanren had discovered his secret of making money through the temple, and asked her to help persuade Yanren. If she could convince Yanren, she would naturally get the money.
On July 26th, as agreed, Yankong brought Zhang Qingzhu to persuade Yanren, with Li Xinyue and Zhao Zhengwei also present. After much persuasion, Yanren still wouldn't relent. Seeing no results, Zhang Qingzhu felt helpless. When she saw Yankong give her a look indicating she should leave first, she departed.
Afterward, Zhang Qingzhu asked Yankong about the results, but Yankong said she hadn't helped at all, so their previous deal couldn't be fulfilled. Zhang Qingzhu was furious. Just as she was about to use the account book to argue, having been deceived for so long, Yankong said that she had no prestige in the temple, so no one would believe anything she said. Moreover, if she dared make a big fuss, Yankong had plenty of money and could easily have her killed.
Zhang Qingzhu was both shocked and angry. She knew Yankong was decisive and ruthless, and she was very worried about being silenced. Deciding to strike first, Zhang Qingzhu bought a type of poison online. This poison was contained in small balls that, when squeezed and burst, would disperse the poison into the air, causing death when inhaled.
On the evening of August 2nd, Zhang Qingzhu prepared some pastries to give to Yankong, planning to use the opportunity to poison him. While preparing, Li Xinyue came to see her, and they chatted casually before Li Xinyue left. Zhang Qingzhu took the pastries to Yankong's room, put them down for him, and pretended to embrace him while he sat on the bed, saying she knew she was wrong and asking him not to be angry. She secretly placed the poison ball under Yankong's pillow - as soon as he slept on the pillow, it would burst the ball and he would die.
[August 3rd Morning]
At 5 AM, Zhang Qingzhu hurried to attend morning prayers, wanting to see if Yankong could still come out alive. She had never attended morning prayers before and didn't know where they were held. She happened to meet Li Xinyue, who was also going to morning prayers, so they walked together. To ease her nervousness, Zhang Qingzhu kept talking to Li Xinyue, but found that Li Xinyue wasn't very willing to respond to her.
When they reached the prayer hall, they found Yankong sitting upright on his meditation cushion. Zhang Qingzhu was disappointed. But after Yankong picked up the wooden fish mallet and prayer beads and began chanting, he suddenly collapsed to the ground after a short while. Those who rushed to check said he had already stopped breathing.
acts_goal: Do not proactively reveal that Hengming also likes to keep dogs.
